## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Who is Achieve, Inc.?

■
 Created by the nation’s governors and
 business leaders, Achieve, Inc., is a
 bipartisan non-profit organization that
 helps states raise academic standards,
 improve assessments and strengthen
 accountability to prepare all young people
 for postsecondary education and training,
 careers, and citizenship.

 2</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">American Diploma Project

■ The American Diploma Project (ADP) was
 created to ensure all graduates leave high
 school ready for college and careers.

■ Early research by ADP sought to identify
 “must-have” knowledge and skills graduates
 will need to be successful in college and the
 workplace.

 3</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">The ADP Benchmarks: Challenging
 content for all students
To cover the content in the ADP benchmarks,
high school graduates need:
■ In Mathematics: ■ In English:
 ● A rigorous four-year ● Four courses
 course sequence ● Content equivalent to
 ● Content* equivalent to four years of grade-
 a sequence that level English or higher
 includes Algebra I and with a strong focus on
 II, Geometry, and Data oral and written
 Analysis &amp; Statistics communication skills
 and considerable
 *can be taught via different research and analysis
 pathways

 4</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">ADP Policy Agenda
■ Align high school standards with college
 and career expectations.
■ Require all students to take curriculum
 aligned with standards.
■ Include “college-ready” tests,
 aligned with state standards, in
 high school assessment system.
■ Hold high schools accountable for
 graduating students college- and career-
 ready, and hold postsecondary institutions
 accountable for student success.

 5</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">ADP Algebra II
 End-of-Course Exam
In 2005, ADP states began to explore possibility
 of collaborating on common assessment goals:
■ To measure “college-ready” content

■ To ensure consistent content and rigor in
 Algebra II courses within and among states
■ To enable comparisons in performance among
 the states
■ To reduce test development costs by working
 together
■ To be considered for postsecondary
 placement purposes
 6</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/07.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Exam Core Content
Operations on Numbers and Expressions
 •Real numbers
 •Complex numbers
 •Algebraic expressions
Equations and Inequalities
 •Linear equations and inequalities
 •Nonlinear equations and inequalities
Polynomial and Rational Functions
 •Quadratic functions
 •Higher-order polynomial and rational functions
Exponential functions
 •Exponential functions
Function Operations and Inverses
 •Function operations and composition
 •Inverse functions
 •Piecewise functions

 7</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/08.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Exam Core Design
■ 57 operational items
■ Two untimed sessions (approximately 90
 minutes each)
■ One with calculator/one without
■ Multiple choice, short answer &amp; extended
 response items
■ At least 30% of points from non-multiple
 choice items
■ Paper &amp; Pencil/Online format
 ● Spring 2008 Paper &amp; Pencil format only

 8</div>
```

<div class="archive-text">Algebra II Exam: Milestones

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/11.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Validity Overview

■ Content Validity
■ Procedural Validity
■ Alignment Evidence
■ College Readiness Evidence-Predictive Validity
 &amp; Concurrent Validity
■ Standard Setting
■ Reporting
■ Consequential Validity

 11</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/12.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">College Readiness

■ College Readiness Evidence
 ● Concurrent Validity
 ◆ What is the relationship between Algebra II and other
 “known” tests (ACT, SAT, placement tests . . .)?
 ● Predictive Validity (Cross-sectional now then longitudinal
 as a cohort reaches college)
 ◆ What is the relationship between Algebra II and success on
 the first semester credit-bearing college course?
 ● Expert Judgment
 ◆ Where do College Professors that teach first semester credit-
 bearing courses believe the readiness cut should be?

 12</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/13.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Standard Setting

■ Different Approach for College Readiness
 ◆ Empirical validity evidence will inform standard setting
 (based on studies previously described)
 ◆ The consortium of states, National Education Leaders, and
 Achieve will serve as the “Board” to review the evidence
 and recommend cut scores. They will use the Briefing
 Book approach.
 ◆ The PLD will have two components: an empirical basis
 based on probability of success in college and descriptions
 of the type of skills that students demonstrate at each level.

 13</div>
```
